chunks: It was narrated from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked him about a man who enters iḥrām in a garment that has an embroidered border, and he said: "There is no harm in it."

key_terms.الْحَلَبِيِّ: al-Ḥalabī, the narrator transmitting this report
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: a garment or piece of clothing
key_terms.عَلَمٌ: a marked or embroidered border on a garment
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters the state of iḥrām for hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to enter iḥrām wearing a garment with an embroidered border?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning clothing worn in the state of iḥrām. It indicates that wearing a garment with an embroidered or marked border is permissible and does not invalidate or compromise the state of iḥrām.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2604 - It was narrated from Al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man entering Ihram wearing a garment with an embroidered border.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it."
